g.textArea: 10A Role-based access and PAM: baseline plus temporary elevation
CTO / developers / QA / DevOps / access owners | Draft | Give each job an agreed baseline and make additional privileged access scoped, eligible and time-bound.

Inputs and the requested change

rect.data-content:
Define teams before access mappings (see 10D)
App developers build products; DevOps builds environments.
QA tests releases; leads/managers/directors provide oversight.
Agree tasks, product boundaries and technical role assignments.

Inventory standing access and existing controls
Review direct/group/inherited grants and current elevation tools.
Identify tasks that need temporary additional privileges.
Current entitlements, configuration and coverage remain to verify.

Request temporary access for an explicit task
The Nov 12 discussion separates default access from elevation.
Read versus write was an example, not a universal role policy.
Agree the smallest useful privilege scope and its owner.

g.textArea: Proposed: maintained baseline and a separate temporary-access path

rect.data-content:
Agreed team / task role
Required work, product and environment.
Assign technical duties explicitly.
Title alone grants no admin access.

Approved membership / mapping
Owned identity group and target mapping.
Joiner/mover/leaver approvals.
Eligibility is separately defined.

Baseline access at the target
Approved role and resource/repo scope.
Maintained while separately authorized.
Normal task follows its existing controls.

Predefined entitlement
Target system, resource scope and roles.
Eligible requesters and approval policy.
Maximum duration and accountable owner.

Eligible user requests a grant
Select entitlement, reason and duration.
Apply configured approval/controls.
Pending or declined requests grant no access.

Temporary access is activated
Verify the target privilege before use.
Record grant ID, start/end and actions.
Use only the approved task and scope.

Entitlement = access definition; grant = one time-bound activation
Expiry or supported revocation ends the temporary grant. Verify the elevated action is denied after propagation; investigate other grants if access remains.
Baseline access continues only while its separate membership/role authorization remains valid.

g.textArea: Expected outcomes
Entitlement catalog fields to agree
Decisions for the team

rect.data-content:
• Normal tasks use understandable baseline permissions.
• Additional privilege has a task, scope and end time.
• Owners can trace who requested, approved and used it.
• Removal is tested and lingering access gets follow-up.

• Meaningful name, purpose, target system and scope.
• Roles, eligible identities/groups and mapping.
• Approval/justification policy and maximum duration.
• Owner, audit, revocation and verification requirements.

• Baseline versus elevated tasks and target systems.
• Eligible requesters, approvals and bounded duration.
• Activation/removal behavior, emergency access and support.
• Remaining standing grants, evidence and review cadence.

Choose and validate an elevation mechanism for each target
Google Cloud: evaluate Google Cloud PAM for selected IAM roles and resource scope using the identity model in 08A.
GitHub: define a separate supported mechanism against 09A. Entra PIM for Groups is a candidate to evaluate; downstream activation/removal and sync delays must be proven. Google Cloud PAM is not a direct GitHub permission grant.

g.textArea: Basis: proposal notes; Nov 12 discussion (07:43–10:37); Google PAM and Entra PIM references checked Nov 16, 2026. Targets, roles, policies and tools remain proposed.

g.data-frame: 10B Temporary elevation: request, authorize, use and verify removal

rect.data-title: 10B Temporary elevation: request, authorize, use and verify removal

g.textArea: 10B Temporary elevation: request, authorize, use and verify removal
Requester / access owners / approvers / elevation service / target operators | Draft | Verify access before the task and verify its removal when the grant ends.
Blue = proposed | Gray = reported context or reference | Yellow = exception, boundary or team decision
Requester / task
Eligibility / authorization
Target activation / checks
Task / grant ending
Verification / audit owners

rect.data-content:
1. Identify a privileged task [Requester]
State target, operation and reason for more access.
Select an approved entitlement and duration.
If baseline is sufficient, use the normal workflow.

Ineligible, declined or request expired
Return the policy/approval outcome to the requester.
Do not activate elevated access.
Correct the request or follow the agreed review path.

Grant creation or activation fails
Track the actual grant/target state; do not assume access is active.
Assigned owners reconcile partial changes and record recovery.
Repeat verification or end the failed grant under the agreed policy.

2. Validate request [Elevation service]
Check requester eligibility and entitlement scope.
Apply reason/duration requirements and limits.
Reject unsupported or out-of-scope requests.

3. Authorize under the entitlement policy
Apply configured approval/control requirements.
Approver(s) decide where the policy requires them.
Pending requests grant no elevated access.

4. Issue a time-bound grant [Elevation service]
Record requester, target, roles and grant start/end.
Proceed only when the configured policy is satisfied.
Track activation, expiry and assigned failure ownership.

Access is not active or scope is wrong
Hold the privileged task; owners check target state.
Check identity, roles and propagation status.
Repeat verification or end the failed grant.

6. Verify effective access [Requester / owner]
Check the approved action on the correct target.
Confirm the grant is active before the task.
Record verification and the remaining time window.

5. Apply target access [Selected mechanism]
Use the target-specific IAM or membership change.
Watch activation state and allow for propagation.
Google Cloud and GitHub implementations are validated separately.

Task fails, overruns or needs early removal
Stop privileged work if the grant ends.
Use a new request for a new access window.
Record failure and use supported revocation as needed.

7. Perform the approved task [Requester]
Use only the authorized operation and scope.
Follow change/review and runbook controls.
Record actions and results during the grant window.

8. End the grant [Service / authorized revoker]
Expiry ends elevation; supported revocation can end it earlier.
Track target removal and propagation under the selected mechanism.
Early task completion follows the agreed early-ending policy.

Removal mismatch: keep follow-up open
If the elevated action still works, reconcile target bindings/membership, sessions and other grants.
Assign an access owner, record the exception and escalate unresolved removal.
Correct the approved scope and repeat the denial check; retain legitimate baseline access only while separately authorized.

9. Verify the end and retain evidence [Owner / service]
Test that elevated access is denied after agreed propagation.
Check remaining grants if the action is still allowed.
Keep baseline only if its separate authorization remains valid.
Retain request, decision, grant, action and removal records.

g.textArea: Proposed target-neutral lifecycle. Approval stages, justification, duration, session/propagation behavior, early-ending capability, support and audit retention require per-target agreement.

rect.data-title: 10C Role-based access and PAM: delivery plan and validation

g.textArea: 10C Role-based access and PAM: delivery plan and validation
Identity / platform and access owners / team leads / QA | Draft | Define baseline and entitlements, prove the complete grant lifecycle, then reduce unnecessary standing privilege.

Proposed work packages

rect.data-content:
1. Define teams and access needs
Use 10D to agree teams and leadership duties.
Map tasks, products and environments.
Inventory standing and overlapping grants.
Define baseline and elevation eligibility.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: Team leads + identity + target owners

rect.data-content:
2. Design a target-specific catalog
Define purpose, roles, scope and eligible identities.
Agree approval, justification and duration policy.
Assign owners, audit and removal requirements.
Choose a supported mechanism for each target.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: Access + identity + platform owners

rect.data-content:
3. Prove one limited entitlement
Test ineligible, pending and declined requests.
Verify active scope before the approved task.
Exercise expiry, supported revocation and delays.
Prove denial afterwards and audit completeness.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: Platform owner + requester/approver + QA

rect.data-content:
4. Expand and review standing access
Roll out reviewed entitlements in controlled scope.
Remove replaced standing grants after validation.
Publish request, support and recovery runbooks.
Review eligibility, usage and lingering access.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: Target + identity owners + team leads
Acceptance evidence before expansion
Inputs and coordination
Operating controls to agree
Open decisions for review

rect.data-content:
• Baseline works; elevated operations are denied before activation.
• Ineligible, pending and declined requests do not gain privilege.
• Active grants permit only the agreed target operation/scope.
• Expiry/revocation removes elevation; valid baseline remains.
• Delays, remaining access, audit and failed-removal escalation are tested.

• Team/task structure and product boundaries from 10D.
• Approved Entra groups and target mappings from 08/09.
• Scoped roles, baseline and separate elevation eligibility.
• Supported target mechanism, accountable owners and pilot.
• Audit from 07 and maintained access catalog through 06.

• Explicit administrators, eligible requesters, approvers and owners.
• Reviewed role/scope changes, justification and bounded duration.
• Verified activation/removal, audit trail and exception ownership.
• Emergency/recovery access and overdue-removal response.
• Recurring eligibility, overlapping-grant and standing-access review.

• Agree app development, DevOps, QA and leadership duties.
• Which product/environment scopes and baseline roles?
• Who owns groups, mappings, eligibility and approvals?
• Which target mechanisms, duration and emergency rules?
• Who verifies removal and maintains the access catalog?

Elevation grants access; the task still follows its normal change and execution controls
Use Google PAM grant lifecycle guidance for the chosen cloud implementation. Prove target activation/removal; group-based downstream access must meet the required timing and scope.
Coordinate 08/09 identity decisions, 01 execution controls and 06/07 documentation/audit operations. Exact roles, target mechanisms, duration, approvals and rollout sequence remain decisions.

g.textArea: Basis: Nov 12 discussion (07:43–10:37) and official Google/Microsoft references checked Nov 16, 2026. This is a proposed model; no entitlement, permission or group configuration is changed.

g.textArea: Access design record for each team / task

rect.data-content:
Team + task + product + environment → approved Entra group → target role and resource/repository scope.
Record group owner, membership rules and mapping; keep baseline separate from elevation eligibility.
For elevation: purpose, eligible identities, roles/scope, approval policy, maximum duration, owner and removal evidence.

Decisions before rollout
Agree team boundaries, reporting relationships, memberships, role names, access owners and approvers. Exact permissions remain to design.
Validate each target integration; test allowed/denied actions, role changes, overlapping grants and removal.
